title: Institutional vs ad-hoc arbitration - what clients should actually choose
p1:
Choosing arbitration does not always mean the dispute will be faster or easier.

Many clients miss one crucial decision: should they choose institutional arbitration or handle everything themselves through ad-hoc arbitration?
p2: A common misconception is that ad-hoc arbitration is always cheaper because there is no institution involved. But without an institution managing timelines, procedures, and administration, parties may spend more time and money handling unexpected issues.
p3:
Institutional arbitration means an established body provides rules, support, and administrative assistance. Ad-hoc arbitration gives parties more flexibility but requires them to manage the process carefully.

The right choice depends on the dispute, complexity, budget, and the level of control parties want. A simple dispute may benefit from flexibility, while a high-value commercial conflict may need structured support.
conclusion: If you were entering a major business contract, would you prefer the flexibility of ad-hoc arbitration or the structured support of institutional arbitration? Why?
